pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with a CHECK on the three values. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' asserts the seeded rows are normal and that setting 'urgent' throws. The harness applies the real migrations before each test.
src/index.js `item()` appends ' — high' or ' — low' and nothing for normal. The 'AC-2' test asserts the exact list items.
src/index.js filters with `WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id`. The 'AC-3' test covers high, low and normal, with ids 1 and 3 in id order.
The unfiltered query is `ORDER BY id`. The 'AC-4' test asserts the full list in id order, and the existing index.test.js tests still pass unchanged.
`nav()` renders the four filters, with the current one as <strong> and the others as links. The 'AC-5' test asserts the exact nav HTML for all four views.
The Set check applies when the param is present, so '', 'High', 'urgent' and '__proto__' all return 400 with no <li>. The 'AC-6' test covers these.

Verified by reading src/index.js lines 59-63: the message is `No

-priority items.` only when the table is non-empty, otherwise 'No items yet.'. The test 'an unmatched filter names its priority; an empty table says No items yet.' covers high, low and normal, and the empty table in all four views.
traffic/routes.json is ["/", "/?priority=high"]. The AC-8 test asserts it. traffic-config-check.mjs now accepts the query, and traffic.test.js sends every ROUTES entry, query included.

findings.what: The README mentions the filter but not that high and low items are labelled after the title, or that every view has an All/High/Normal/Low nav.
findings.fix: Add a short clause about the labels and the filter nav to the `src/index.js` bullet.

lenses.note: Spec specs/item-priority.md exists. The change matches its intent and decisions, and adds nothing beyond it except the traffic-check query allowance the new route needs.
All 8 acceptance items are met. The decisions on normal as the default and labelling only high and low are followed.
test/priority.test.js asserts behaviour for each AC and state. No tests were deleted or loosened. The traffic fake app and traffic-config test were extended.
The README was updated for the filter. The labels and nav are not described (low finding).
Parameterised query, a Set allowlist, escaped titles. No defects found. I could not run the tests because Bash was refused, so this is a read-only review.
The priority input is allowlisted and bound as a parameter. Only fixed filter values are interpolated into HTML. No planted instructions found.
The diff changes the HTML page in src/index.js, but no browser was available and the spec has no visual requirements beyond the text and nav checked by tests.
The page changes in src/index.js. I could not run it, but the HTML output is asserted by tests.
The title is under 72 characters. The claims match the diff: behaviour, migration, route, traffic-check relaxation and tests.
